goal: Language-agnosticism #37: body_field() + noise_node_types() delegation in clusters/profile, unblocking the receiver-density signal on flat-body languages (Julia/Ruby)

summary.title: Language-agnosticism #37: body_field delegation + interior-only ngram
summary.what: clusters._body_roots resolves the walkable callable body from grammar facts (named body_field() child -> block_types() wrapper for Ruby's body_statement -> flat-body direct children minus body_skip_types() for Julia), replacing the hardcoded child_by_field_name('body') in _bodies_index. profile._signature_ngrams now keeps only interior nodes (child_count > 0) instead of the Python-specific _LEAF_OR_NOISE set; _signature_ngrams and _receiver_call_count walk a list of body roots. test_receiver_density gains Julia (flat-body) + Ruby cases. Suite 204->206.
summary.why: The hardcoded 'body' field returned None for Julia's function_definition (no body field), so _bodies_index silently dropped every Julia callable, leaving its receiver-density signal dark -- the same 'not flagged == clean' overfit class as #34/#36. The _LEAF_OR_NOISE set only listed Python's leaf/literal node types, so every other language's leaf tokens (int_literal, :=, func, end, integer_literal) leaked into the structural body-shape signature.
summary.user_goal: Language-agnosticism #37: body_field() + noise_node_types() delegation in clusters/profile, unblocking the receiver-density signal on flat-body languages (Julia/Ruby)

decisions.point: How to reach the callable body when body_field() is empty (flat-body languages)
decisions.chose: A neutral _body_roots(node, grammar) helper: body_field() child, else a block_types() wrapper child, else flat direct-children minus body_skip_types()
decisions.rationale: The resolution logic is language-neutral and consumes only existing grammar facts (body_field/block_types/body_skip_types), so it stays a shared helper rather than a new per-grammar override. It returns a list of roots so a flat-body language with no single wrapper node (Julia) is handled uniformly with braced languages.
rejected: Treating empty body_field() as 'walk the whole callable node' (would fold the signature/keyword tokens into the body-shape signature)

decisions.point: Whether Ruby is a flat-body language that was being dropped (per the pre-compaction note)
decisions.chose: No -- corrected by direct probe; only Julia was dropped
decisions.rationale: Ruby's method node exposes a body field (-> body_statement), so child_by_field_name('body') already reached it. The note that both Julia and Ruby were dark was half wrong. Ruby is still routed correctly here via the block_types() branch and kept as a regression case.
rejected: Trusting the summary's claim that Ruby was also dropped

decisions.point: noise_node_types() as a per-grammar fact vs a universal property
decisions.chose: Universal: keep only interior nodes (child_count > 0); did NOT add a noise_node_types() grammar fact
decisions.rationale: A node carries structural shape iff it has children; leaves are tokens. This needs zero per-grammar enumeration and cannot silently leak when a new grammar is added -- strictly more agnostic than a fact each grammar must remember to populate. Deviates from the work-list's literal 'noise_node_types() fact' wording but serves its goal (de-overfit the ngram noise) more completely. Verified test_profile_detects_missing_class (Python body_jaccard>=0.7) still holds.
rejected: A noise_node_types() classmethod with per-grammar literal/keyword enumeration (fragile; silent leak on a forgotten grammar)

rejected.reason: The universal interior-only ngram rule de-overfits more completely with zero per-grammar surface and no silent-leak failure mode.
body_field() is also consumed by the complexity walker; the block_types() route reaches Ruby's body_statement without risking that walk, and the suite stays green.
